News.title: Farage's by-election victory won't stop questions about finances
News.content:
Nigel Farage did not turn up to savour his victory in the by-election he triggered himself.

Overnight he told a rally of Reform UK supporters he had been advised there was an "organised campaign to disrupt and degrade the result" and wanted to avoid being "demeaned and humiliated by nobodies".

When the official result did come in hours later, it confirmed the Reform UK leader had indeed won this by-election convincingly with 22,239 votes, but without any serious opposition after the other main parties did not put up candidate.

Farage's allies say he has been both emboldened and re-energised by this race, and it is not difficult to work out why.

He is clearly popular in the constituency, his party has had a commanding lead in national opinion polls for much of the past 18 months, and he has achieved something remarkable in turning his upstart organisation into a mass-membership movement with a serious chance of getting into government.

But today's result won't stop the Metropolitan Police investigation into donations to Reform UK, questions about Farage's friendship with a convicted fraudster, or the parliamentary investigation into why he did not register a Â£5m gift from a billionaire donor.

And given Farage triggered this race and the result was entirely predictable, what was the point of it all?

When he made his surprise announcement last month that he was resigning to run for a seat he already represented, the Reform leader said "the people of Clacton should be the judges of my actions" - and he wanted to "fight to continue the political revolution that Reform has started".

Could he have predicted that continuing his "revolution" would descend into a bizarre electoral battle involving a record 34 candidates, a 90cm long ballot paper, with his most prominent challenger being a man dressed as a bin?

Labour say Farage has been trying to "dodge scrutiny", and the Conservatives argue he triggered this race because he was having a "hissy fit".

One thing the Reform UK leader could have anticipated is the cost. In a constituency with the most deprived neighbourhood in England, the council estimates taxpayers will need to fork out Â£250,000 for the organisation of this by-election. Reform UK has offered to foot the bill, but that is not allowed under electoral law.

Now the election is over, Farage is likely to face renewed scrutiny on those outstanding questions about his finances.

News.title: NHS service admits data breach due to pager use
News.content:
The sensitive medical data of transplant patients from across the UK was routinely sent over an unencrypted pager network, an NHS service has admitted.

A BBC investigation found NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) sent the names, dates of birth and types of organs being offered or needed to members of hospital transplant teams who were using pagers, unaware they were not encrypted.

In 2019, then-Health Secretary Matt Hancock announced the NHS in England should stop using pagers by 2021, but some parts of the organisation have continued doing so.

NHSBT said it was "deeply sorry" and has reported the data breach to the Information Commissioner. It added it has now stopped sending patient data in this way.

Pagers are small battery operated radio receivers - popular in the 1980s and 1990s - that can receive short text messages, numbers to call, or alerts.

They are a one-way communication system and only able to receive messages, not send them, which was why they largely fell out of public use as more and more people started carrying mobile phones.

News.title: Final day of heatwave for many before weekend cooldown
News.content:
Kew Gardens in London reached 38.1C on Thursday, making it the UK's hottest day of 2026 so far, and the fifth hottest UK day on record.

It is also the second time this year that the temperature has reached 38C, after Lingwood, Norfolk recorded 38.0C on 26 June.

This is only the second time that 38C has been reached twice in the same year - the previous occasion being 2022.

Though the Met Office amber warning for extreme heat that covered large swathes of England on Thursday expired at midnight, high temperatures will linger in central and eastern parts of England on Friday.

Long spells of sunshine will lift temperatures to 29-34C (84-93F) across large parts of the Midlands, Lincolnshire, East Anglia and the south-east.

For many places it will mark a third consecutive day above official heatwave thresholds.

The heat will ease elsewhere.

Somewhat cooler conditions will begin to move into northern and western parts of the UK, although temperatures will generally remain above the norm for the time of year - widely reaching the low to mid-20s Celsius.

Many places will be dry with a mix of cloud and sunny spells although a few showers are possible, and these could be heavy and thundery in some places.

News.title: New Zealand break with Oceania Football Confederation to withdraw Infantino support
News.content:
New Zealand have broken rank with Oceania's football governing body to become the latest nation to withdraw support for Fifa president Gianni Infantino.

Infantino has lost support from three regional confederations - Europe's Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and Concacaf (North and Central America and the Caribbean) - over his aborted plans to sell 20% of the World Cup's commercial rights to private investors.

The Confederation of African Football (Caf) and South American governing body Conmebol have backed the 56-year-old to win a fourth presidential term at the Fifa Congress in March.

New Zealand have followed several individual member nations including England, Wales, Norway, the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland in confirming they will not support Infantino's re-election bid.

"New Zealand Football is also seeking an independent review of the steps undertaken to develop the Fifa Forward Enterprise Scheme (FFE)," a statement read.

"After careful consideration, NZF has formed the view that decisions and actions within FIFA have contributed to a breakdown in trust and increased division within international football, and that an independent review is required to restore confidence and trust.

"NZF believes this point in time represents an opportunity for all Fifa member associations to advocate for stronger governance, accountability and transparency which are fundamental in maintaining confidence of the administration of the global game."

New Zealand was the only one of the OFC's 11 members to qualify for the 2026 Fifa World Cup.

NZF chief executive Andrew Pragnell said: "We've called for an independent review specifically because what we don't want to see is a sort of in-house quick washover of this.

"An independent review is something else that has been called for by other confederations that will help restore some of the trust."

The Oceania Football Confederation said it welcomed Fifa's decision to withdraw the proposal, but stopped short of declaring or withdrawing support for Infantino.

"The OFC Executive Committee welcomes Fifa's decision to withdraw the FFE proposal and its commitment to review the issues surrounding the project," the statement said.

"The OFC recognises the progress achieved over the last decade in advancing football development in Oceania under Fifa's leadership and encourages Fifa to use the review as an opportunity to identify and implement any changes that may be necessary."

News.title: How a major oil slick started washing up on Iran's beaches
News.content:
Verified videos show a major oil slick washing up on Iran's Qeshm Island, which analysts have said comes from a ship hit by a strike in the Strait of Hormuz.

BBC Verify has also analysed satellite imagery suggesting the oil spill originated from an attack on a vessel in Omani waters on 3 August. A week later, the apparent fuel leakage from the Minoan Pioneer bulk carrier had spread across a large area of the strait.

Environmental experts say the spill threatens wildlife, protected ecosystems and fishing communities around Qeshm, which is home to mangrove forests, nearby coral reef habitats and nesting sites for critically endangered Hawksbill turtles.

Iranian media initially reported the origin of the pollution was under investigation and Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said on Thursday its source was a "foreign bulk ship".

A local environmental protection official has since said the spill has been "almost completely cleaned up". BBC Verify has not been able to independently confirm this.

News.title: 'Two out of four, baby' - Hunt wins 200m as she eyes historic quadruple
News.content:
Britain's Amy Hunt charged to 200m glory to secure her second gold medal of the European Championships - but the sprinter has her sights set on a historic quadruple in Birmingham.

The 24-year-old wants to "be iconic" and become the first athlete to win four European gold medals in the same tournament.

And after triumphing in the 100m on Monday, she added another gold to her collection with a season's best time of 22.19 seconds in the 200m final on Thursday.

Hunt reeled in rival and compatriot Asher-Smith down the back straight to cross the line first.

"Two out of four, baby!" Hunt told BBC TV.

"This is becoming a magical week and one I will remember for the rest of my life."

Hunt is set to compete in the women's and mixed 4x100m relay events later and says there will be "no celebrations and no champagne until Sunday night".

"I have got a debt to the ladies," she said.

"We have got to come out here and make sure we show them who the best sprinting nation is in Europe."

Asher-Smith was beaten to silver by just 0.01 seconds by Ireland's Rhasidat Adeleke, who set a new national record.

"It unfolded exactly how I thought it would," two-time European 200m silver medallist Nethaneel Mitchell-Blake said on BBC Radio 5 Live.

"I knew Dina would run a blistering bend and then say 'Amy, come and catch me'. And that's what Amy has done."

News.title: BBC Verify speaks to woman who filmed ICE agent pointing gun at her
News.content:
A video showing a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent pointing his gun at a woman has been viewed by millions after she shared the moment on Instagram.

Carolina Molina says she was out delivering business cards in Falls Church, Virginia, when she saw ICE agents, who then surrounded her car.

The US Department of Homeland Security said she "attempted to harm officers by weaponising her vehicle". Molina denies this.

BBC Verify assesses the dashcam footage shared by Molina. Jake Horton reports.

News.title: 'She was just Gaynor from up the road' - villagers ready for emotional Bonnie Tyler goodbye
News.content:
There aren't many villages where you can walk into a jewellers, a hardware shop, or a cafe, and hear stories about one of the world's biggest music icons.

But in Mumbles, Swansea, Bonnie Tyler was never treated like a superstar.

To many local people, she was Gaynor Sullivan, or "Gaynor who lived up the road".

The Total Eclipse of the Heart singer, who died in July aged 75, would often be seen doing her shopping or having a drink with friends.

On Wednesday it seemed only fitting that the iconic song could be heard playing throughout the village as the biggest partial solar eclipse in nearly three decades took place, with Spotify streams of it almost doubling.

As locals prepare to say goodbye to Tyler, who split her time between the Mumbles and a home in Portugal, it's ordinary moments that people seem to remember most.

On Saturday, hundreds of people are expected to line the streets of Newton Road to pay their respects, as Tyler's coffin makes its way through the village to her home on Mumbles Road.

A service will then be held in St Mary's Church in Swansea city centre on Monday, for family and invited guests, before the cortege makes its way to her birthplace of Skewen, Neath Port Talbot.

News.title: Ice cream man hit with noise complaint over van's music
News.content:
An ice cream man has been hit with a noise complaint by someone who did not like the loud chimes from his van.

Mark Edwards was contacted by the council after a Tonyrefail resident complained about the van's music being played in the evening.

He said he had been serving the area for more than 20 years without a complaint and was determined "not to let one individual spoil it for everybody else". He has agreed with customers to beep his horn in each street so they know he is there.

Rhondda Cynon Taf council said it received a noise complaint in June relating to music being played after 20:00 BST, which it investigated and found to be valid.

Edwards, from Trebanog, said he was taken aback when he found a letter from the council on the van's dashboard: "Twenty-odd years and I have never had anything like this at all. It's unbelievable."

He said his employer told him to stop operating in the area because continuing to use the chimes could result in a fine, but he did not want to stop serving customers, so came up with the alternative plan.

"I thought 'I'm not going to let one individual to spoil it for everybody else', so have come to an arrangement with my customers in the area.

"They know roughly what time I'm there and I toot the horn in each street, and they all come out and enjoy it. They're not going to beat me."

The council said the law required a 19:00 cut-off time for ice cream van operators to use their chimes, but it did not "prevent them from trading after this time".

It added that Edwards had been sent a letter reminding him of these requirements and that it considered the matter closed.

News.title: It's in my soul - actor brings small town novel to big screen
News.content:
While the story itself is a work of fiction, McMenamin said the world of Skintown is very much based on his own personal experiences of a teenager growing up during the Troubles in Northern Ireland and trying to escape that.

"The world is mine, and that of my friends we grew up in," he explained.

"The escapism of the rave, and the communities, the kids coming together and realising that they have more in common than they thought.

"It is a work of fiction but there is a lot of me in it."

The soundtrack will also help transport the audience back in time with Prodigy, Elastica, Happy Mondays and Carl Cox featuring.

Despite starring Derry Girls' O'Donnell and Tara Lynne O'Neill, McMenamin said that's where the comparisons end with Lisa McGee's hit show, which was also set during the same period in Northern Ireland.

"The humour is the same," he said. "If we've landed anything half as well as Lisa McGee, we will be over the moon.

"It's the same era and some of the humour will definitely be the same tone â as that's our sense of humour.

"That's the thing about the film I'm proudest about - the humour.

"There's a lot of the film which is very serious, it has a very serious message and it's quite a heavy drama at times but it's also a good night out and the boys in it are brilliant. It's good fun."

News.title: Top grades rise again as students get A-level, T-level and BTec results
News.content:
Hundreds of thousands of students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland have opened their A-level, T-level and BTec results on Thursday morning.

The percentage of top A-level grades edged up again, and a record number of students found out they had secured a place at university.

The cost of going to university has been in the spotlight this year, with mounting pressure on the government to reform student loan repayments, and there has been a renewed focus on technical education under Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

But the chief executive of Universities UK, which represents more than 140 vice-chancellors, urged students to not "let politicians make your decision for you".

The percentage of A* and A grades at A-level increased to 28.5% across England, Wales and Northern Ireland this year, up from 28.3% last year.

About 40% of 18-year-olds in England receive A-levels every summer.

Around 250,000 grades for vocational and technical qualifications were also released to students in England.

These include BTec National, Cambridge Technical, Cambridge Advanced National and T-level results.

Almost 20,000 students completed a T-level in 2026, with a pass rate of over 90%.

Launched in 2020, T-levels are two-year technical courses that are taken after GCSEs. They focus more on practical subjects than academic ones, but are an equivalent qualification to three A-levels.

AS-levels, which will count towards students' final A-level results next summer in Wales and Northern Ireland, have also been released.

This year, the pass rate for National 5, Higher and Advanced Higher exams in Scotland rose across the board.

News.title: Son of 102-year-old says father died after being 'pushed off stage'
News.content:
Robert said: "He just asked them to turn the music down."

He said his father turned around to come back down off the stage when he was pushed, and that resulted in a broken hip.

"[That's] the most upsetting part. He wasn't going to live forever but it's not a nice way, obviously in pain," he said.

"We want to see justice, of course.

"They must have known he was an old man. It makes you wonder what the world is coming to.

"It has obviously made it difficult. It would've been nice if he'd gone quietly in his sleep.

"He was in hospital, suffering, for a week-and-a-half. It's not nice.

"I feel sad - even though he could be difficult because of his age and dementia, still, you get used to him being around," he said.

Robert, a retired civil engineer, said his father used to visit the Crow's Nest.

"What happened is not nice. The pub has changed a lot over the years. It has become a youngsters' pub," he said.

Robert said he grew up in the home in the the Llanyrafon neighbourhood where his father had lived since 1960.

He said his dad had a career as a design draughtsman and had lived alone since his wife died 40 years ago.

"Me and my brother would visit our father regularly, and clean the house and buy him food.

"His eyesight had deteriorated and he had been diagnosed with dementia two or three years ago."

Robert said: "He's well-known around here, although a lot of his generation are gone," he added.

He said his father would visit the pub two or three times a week, where he would drink beers, and described how he became a familiar face to some locals.

"I suppose he became a pub character," he added.

News.title: Couple tie the knot on 'magical' solar eclipse day
News.content:
Wednesday's full eclipse may be something many of us remember for a long time: the special glasses, the colanders, and the eerie shadowing of the sun.

And for one couple, it was especially unforgettable as they got married during the once-in-a-generation event.

Jerry and Jamie Bone, from Gosfield, Essex, planned their big day around the astronomical phenomenon - the first total solar eclipse visible over mainland Europe since 1999 - and tied the knot in Alpheton, near Sudbury, Suffolk.

Jamie said they had realised a few years ago the eclipse would take place in 2026, and decided it would be the "perfect" day to get married.

News.title: Bonnie Tyler's classic hit spiked in streams during solar eclipse
News.content:
Born Gaynor Hopkins in a council house in Neath, Tyler grew up with a love for music before she was discovered by talent scout Roger Bell in a Swansea club.

Tyler released her first single, Lost in France in 1977, but it was the release of Total Eclipse of the Heart five years later which changed her life.

The ballad spent two weeks at UK number one and four weeks in the US.

The iconic love song's music video surpassed 1.2 billion views on YouTube and has had over a billion streams on Spotify.

Spotify previously said it had paid out more than $1.4 million for streams of Tyler's catalogue in 2025.

The music platform said Total Eclipse of the Heart was one of a few "celestial" songs that saw a streaming spike in the UK on 12 August.

According to Spotify, the biggest increases in UK streams during the eclipse were:

Evolfo, Moon Eclipsed the Sun (+12,817%)

Chris Staples, Dark Side of the Moon (+2,805%)

Pink Floyd, Eclipse (+594%)

Delta Goodrem, Eclipse (+104%)

Bonnie Tyler, Total Eclipse of the Heart (+94%)

Bill Withers, Ain't No Sunshine (+17%)

Shannon Carragher, senior editor at Spotify, said: "It is always fascinating to see how major cultural events instantly reflect in what the UK is listening to.

"Cultural phenomena like the solar eclipse naturally bring people together and we instinctively look for the perfect soundtrack to share that moment."

Ahead of the solar eclipse, Tyler's McVitie's Jaffa Cakes TV advert also resurfaced - it was originally broadcast in 2023 when there was a partial lunar eclipse.

The nostalgic advert came after research revealed almost half (49%) of Brits did not understand how eclipses occurred.

In the video, Tyler uses a Jaffa Cake as a prop to describe the different types of eclipse.

She said: "There are three types of eclipse. You've got the lunar eclipse, the solar eclipse, and then there's the total eclipse of the heart.

"When the earth is situated between the moon and the sun it creates a shadow, and when it looks like someone has just taken a bite out of the moon. That's a partial lunar eclipse."

The grammy-nominated star had a string of other hits, including Holding out for a Hero and also represented the UK at the Eurovision Song Contest in 2013.

She was named in the Queen's last Birthday Honours list in 2022 and was awarded an MBE for her services to music by Prince William the following year.

Tyler died "unexpectedly" on 8 July, aged 75, at a Portugal hospital, "as a result of the illness that she was being treated for", her family said in a statement released on the star's official website, external.

At the time, tributes poured in from a host of friends and stars including Catherine Zeta-Jones, Bryan Adams and Rod Stewart.

Tyler's funeral service will take place on 17 August at 12:00 BST at St Mary's Church in Swansea.

It has since been confirmed that her coffin will be brought to her Mumbles home on 15 August at 15:30 BST.

People are invited to "pay their respects" by lining Newton Road at 15:15 BST.

News.title: Honeytrap thieves jailed for killing men they had drugged
News.content:
A couple who drugged men seeking sexual services in order to steal from them have been jailed for killing two men and poisoning others.

Adina Mihai and Madalin Dumitru admitted the manslaughter of Gary Mouat, 37, from Oxfordshire, and Malcolm King, 80, from Gloucestershire, in 2025 and 2024 respectively.

On the first day of their trial in June, the pair also each admitted two further counts of administering poison to surviving victims.

Mihai, 31, and Dumitru, 30, were both sentenced to 17 years in prison at Oxford Crown Court.

Mihai, who posed as a sex worker, and her partner Dumitru, arranged to meet men paying for services she had advertised online at their homes.

The court heard four had their alcoholic drinks spiked with the powerful sedative gamma-butyrolactone (GBL) so the pair could steal from them.

Two men died as a result, while two others - who cannot be named due to reporting restrictions - survived.

News.title: Big Issue says vendors struggling as sales hit by heatwaves
News.content:
Big Issue vendors are struggling to sell magazines in the UK's extreme heat, which is having an "immediate" impact on their earnings, Big Issue's managing director says.

Sales of the British news and entertainment magazine are down on average 20% year on year in weeks where heatwaves have been declared, Catherine Parsons said.

During June's record-breaking temperatures, the worst-hit West Midlands and Wales saw 34% and 33% fewer sales respectively.

George Anderson, who sells the Big Issue near the BBC's Broadcasting House in London, says it is a struggle when footfall is lower and people would rather be near the aircon.

"People are uncomfortable, they don't want to hang around in the heat and chat," he told the BBC on the hottest day of the year.

"I manage it as best I can, and so far so good, but my sales are definitely down which can be quite tough."

Big Issue is sold by people experiencing homelessness or financial instability.

But Parsons said sellers are losing out on vital income due to the heatwaves.

"For most of us, extreme heat is an inconvenience. For Big Issue vendors, it means earning significantly less and making difficult decisions about rent, food and other essentials," she said.

In the week of 22 June, when the UK's June temperature record was broken and temperatures hit 37.7C (99.9F), Big Issue sales fell by an average of 22% compared to the same week the previous year, their figures show.

The latest spell of extreme heat marks the UK's fifth heatwave this year, with the Met Office warning this summer is on course to be the UK's hottest since records began.

Parsons said Big Issue teams were working to support vendors and had been handing out sunscreen, caps and water bottles.

"But in the most extreme temperatures, it's simply unsafe for vendors to be out and selling, and when the heat forces them to cut their working day short, the financial impact is immediate."

News.title: Transfer news LIVE: Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez deadline looms, Arsenal eye up shock Osimhen move, Rodri exit latest
News.content:
Chelsea have told Manchester City that they have until 5pm today to submit a bid for midfielder Enzo Fernandez. The Blues have informed their Premier League rivals that they will need to sepnd £120m to sign the Argentina though City had hoped to negotiate on the price.

City, meanwhile, remain in talks with Barcelona over Rodri, who is available for £60m. The club have rejected two previous bids for the former Ballon d’Or winner but talks are ongoing. City are also interested in signing World Cup breakout star Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille while Savinho is moving closer to leaving the Etihad for Tottenham in a £65m deal though.

Mikel Arteta has said that Arsenal’s business is not done yet, with the Gunners receiving interest in Gabriel Martinelli from Galatasaray. The availability of Victor Osimhen has been raised in those talks, although Arsenal have also been linked with moves for Atletico Madrid’s Julian Alvarez and Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola.

Barcola also leads Liverpool’s list of transfer targets and the Reds are in talks with PSG over a fee, though the European champions are demanding £145m to sell the winger. PSG chairman Nasser Al-Khelaifi did not rule out an exit for Barcola, however, saying: “We’re working calmly, we don’t talk too much. I can’t say whether he will leave or not. Today, he is a PSG player. We’ll see.”

More than one million people have signed a petition to block two of PC Andrew Harper’s killers from being released from prison early following huge public outcry.

Thames Valley Police Federation (TVPF) launched the petition last week, condemning the government’s decision not to include the killers in exceptions from a new early prison scheme as “outrageous”.

PC Harper, 28, was responding to reports of a quad bike theft in Berkshire in 2019 when he was caught in a strap attached to the back of a car and dragged down a country road as three teenage suspects fled the scene.

Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were sentenced to 13 years for manslaughter, are set to be freed in January - half way through their sentences - under existing plans.

Downing Street has faced significant backlash after it announced some offenders, including the most serious sex offenders, would be exempt from plans to release some prisoners early - but did not include those who have killed first responders.

open image in gallery PC Andrew Harper was killed while on duty in 2019 ( PA Media )

On Tuesday, prime minister Andy Burnham said he is “increasingly confident” that work to increase space in the prison system “will allow us to reduce the number of people released early and, in the case of the most serious offenders like those convicted of the killing of PC Harper, prevent their early release altogether”.

Mr Burnham said justice secretary Alex Norris will now look at ways to keep “a greater number of the most serious offenders” behind bars and will announce the plans when Parliament returns in September.

In the petition, Aileen O'Connor, chair of the TVPF, said the government’s decision “pours salt into wounds that have never healed”.

open image in gallery Pc Andrew Harper’s mother Debbie Adlam said a Downing Street official had spoken to her (Jacob King/PA) ( PA Archive )

“It is an insult to Andrew's family, his friends, his colleagues and the entire policing family,” she added.

The petition has attracted hundreds of comments from supporters, including from current and former officers.

“As an ex TVP officer, it disgusts me the lack of support towards officers, one wrote. “Officers put their life or the line day in, day out and should be going back to their families at the end of the shift. It should be life for life no matter the circumstances but taking a life of an emergency service worker and getting released early is not definitely not okay. I am so angry and my heart goes out to all of his family.”

Another added: “No family should have to face this, least of all the family of a man dedicated to protecting us.”

PC Harper’s mother said she had received a call from Downing Street on Monday night and has “got a little bit of hope that we didn’t have before” that the killers will not be released early.

Discussing the call she had with a member of the prime minister’s staff, Debbie Adlam told BBC Breakfast: “She said that he wanted to convey that he wants to do everything that he can and has more hope now of finding a resolution to this to try and keep them in prison.

“I think the fact that it’s actually come from Downing Street – I’ve got to try and have some faith in it but, at the same time, I have to protect my own feelings.”

But she added: “It feels like a hash. It feels like a rush job. It feels like nobody’s put enough effort into actually look for reasons or ways.

“We are having to push on every level, and it just doesn’t feel like, as a British citizen, I shouldn’t be doing this. They weren’t given extreme sentences, and I’m only asking for them to do what they were given.”

A Ministry of Justice spokesperson previously said: “The death of PC Andrew Harper was a horrific crime. Our thoughts are with his family and friends, and we share the anger from the police community that we are in this position.

“Thanks to tireless campaigning by Andrew’s family, Harper’s Law means that anyone convicted of killing an emergency worker whilst committing a crime now gets a mandatory life sentence. This government has gone further by introducing a presumption that anyone convicted of murdering a police, prison or probation officer is handed a whole-life order.

“We have been clear that we wanted to go further and block more offenders from getting out sooner into their sentence but could not do so without risking prisons reaching capacity and collapsing.

“If that happened, police could not make arrests, courts could not remand offenders and there would be unchecked criminality on our streets.”

News.title: Count Binface responds to Farage after finishing second in Clacton by-election
News.content:
Count Binface said that he is feeling “gratified” after he came second in the Clacton by-election.

Nigel Farage won with 22,239 votes, triggering the by-election after he resigned as an MP amid ongoing scrutiny of his financial affairs.

Speaking from Clacton on Friday (14 August), Count Binface, the satirical alter ego of comedian Jonathan David Harvey, expressed his happiness with the result.

Count Binface, who received 9,455 votes, said he attended the count “to get the verdict of the good people of Clacton”, which he said was the “least he could do”.

Mr Farage did not appear after he claimed that Essex Police informed him about a threat against him. The Independent understands that the force did not advise the Reform UK leader to stay away.

Nicole Kidman is sharing a rare look back on her decade-long marriage to Tom Cruise.

The Oscar-winning legend, 59, reflected on her life in the spotlight in a British Vogue profile published Thursday, in which she said she became comfortable with fame quickly because of her marriage to Cruise, which lasted from 1990 to 2001.

“You have to remember literally, because of who I married at such a young age, I was thrust into it since I was 22,” she told the magazine. “Suddenly I was 22, 23 years old and I had this huge movie star husband. But it just seemed completely natural. We just fell madly in love and it was that simple.”

She continued, “I remember people saying to me, ‘OK, well this is really going to affect your career.’ I’m like, ‘I don’t care. I’m in love. I want to be married.’ And then I was his ‘wife’ and they were like, ‘See, we told you.’ I’m like, ‘So what? I wasn’t meant to marry the man I love? Of course I’ll throw my career away. I don’t care.’”

Cruise, 64, and Kidman met on the set of the 1990 movie Days of Thunder and were married later that year. Together, the former couple adopted children Isabella and Connor and starred in three movies together: Days of Thunder, Far and Away and Eyes Wide Shut.

open image in gallery Nicole Kidman has shared a rare comment about her previous marriage to Tom Cruise ( Getty )

They ultimately divorced in 2001, citing irreconcilable differences.

After the split, Kidman’s career in Hollywood continued to thrive with projects like Moulin Rouge!, The Hours, Bewitched, Big Little Lies, Being the Ricardos, Babygirl and Lioness. She went on to win an Oscar for The Hours in 2003.

In her personal life, she married country singer Keith Urban in 2006, with whom she shares two children: Sunday Rose, 18, and Faith, 15. Urban and Kidman were together for 19 years before separating in 2025. They finalized their divorce in January.

open image in gallery Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman were married from 1990 to 2001 ( AFP/Getty Images )

Cruise went on to marry Katie Holmes; they remained together from 2006 to 2012.

Kidman has reflected on the whirlwind nature of her first marriage before. In a 2016 interview with Red magazine, she said about tying the knot with the Top Gun actor at age 23: “I was so young when I got married. I look back now and I’m like, ‘What?’”

“You look at Taylor Swift, I mean how old is she? She’s 26. I had two kids by the time I was 27 and I’d been married for four years. But that’s what I wanted,” she said at the time.

News.title: ‘More pain’ to come after economic slowdown
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. The economy grew at a slower pace in the second quarter of the year, official figures show, under pressure from the Iran war.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 0.4pc between April and June, down from 0.6pc in the first three months of the year, according to the Office for National Statistics.

The figures underline the challenge that the conflict poses for Andy Burnham, who has pledged to deliver “growth in every postcode”.

The Prime Minister has already been warned that the economy will slow further next year if Donald Trump continues his war in the Middle East.

Treasury officials have predicted UK growth of just 0.3pc in 2027 if the Strait of Hormuz stays blocked for the rest of this year.

That is far lower than the 1.6pc predicted by the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) in March, based on assumptions made before the start of the war. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Iran war threatens to cripple growth, Treasury warns Burnham | Officials predict economic expansion of just 0.3pc in 2027 if Strait of Hormuz stays blocked

2) Britain facing £54bn bill for North Sea shutdown | Costs soar amid shortage of specialised ships needed to clear up abandoned oil rigs

3) Ban on zero-hours contracts to cost companies up to £3bn | Businesses face huge bill to offer workers guaranteed hours under Employment Rights Act

4) Nvidia’s AI push has echoes of Enron, says Big Short investor | Michael Burry claims chip giant is engaging in ‘circular’ financing

5) Shadow bank founder battles to stave off bankruptcy threat | Paresh Raja launches legal claim to prevent administrators from chasing him for repayment

What happened overnight

Asian shares were mostly higher, powered by gains for AI-related stocks including computer chips as regional markets tracked a rally on Wall Street.

Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 advanced 1.6pc to 68,601.21. In South Korea, the Kospi jumped 4pc, climbing to 6,844.65, as shares in Samsung Electronics surged 5.4pcc. Computer chipmaker SK Hynix jumped 7.1pc.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng rose 0.3pc to 3,967.28, while the Shanghai Composite index added 0.5pc to 3,967.65.

In Australia, the S&P/ASX 200 slipped 0.4pc to 9,155.80.

Data from the US on Wednesday showed consumer prices had risen in line with analysts’ expectations in July.

Wall Street stocks were boosted on Wednesday by gains made by tech companies CoreWeave and Super Micro Computer, both of which closed up by more than 19pc.

The Nasdaq Composite ended the session up 0.5pc, with the S&P 500 up nearly 0.3pc. The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished the session marginally down.

Oil prices were little changed as investors weighed the deadlock in talks between the US and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, was broadly flat at nearly $89 a barrel.

News.title: H5N1 sparks a very Australian epidemic
News.content:
H5N1 bird flu has reached Australia’s shores and is threatening to infect some of the country’s most unique wildlife.

Australasia is the last continent to be hit by the highly infectious avian influenza H5N1, a new strain of which has been circulating worldwide since 2020.

Since recording its first case in June, more than 200 wild seabirds in Australia have been infected, with fears that the highly infectious flu could quickly ‘jump’ to other species.

While H5N1 has infected animals from foxes to sea lions in other parts of the world in recent years, the epidemic now threatens some of Australia’s most iconic wildlife – many of which are found nowhere else on earth.

An Australian government assessment of more than 2,000 native species warned that nearly one in five faces a high risk from the deadly H5N1 bird flu, with hundreds of unique birds and mammals vulnerable to severe population reductions or even extinction.

Those animals include iconic species like the Tasmanian devils, quolls, and dingoes.

Other aquatic mammals, including the platypus, which is only found in Australia, are at risk of infection through contact with bird droppings in shared wetlands and coastal environments.

News.title: Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end
News.content:
Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

News.title: Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG
News.content:
His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

News.title: Advice, cookbooks and emergency pot noodles: Your best gifts for university students
News.content:
When it comes to sending a child or grandchild off to university, it can be tempting to fill their room with every conceivable gadget.

So to help, we asked the Telegraph Recommended Community for their best gift recommendations and their suggestions ranged from desk lamps to cookery books and supermarket gift cards.

Here are the essentials worth buying.

Kitchen basics

From cupboard essentials to electrical appliances and cookbooks, most readers say they’d gift kitchen equipment.

Thinking back to his university days, reader TJ, 43, from London, says “the main essentials are around kitchen items and good long lasting food”.

“It’s nice to have some bits to cook for others as well and to make friends quickly,” he adds.

Susan, 54, from the West Midlands, agrees, recommending “basic cooking equipment” as a key staple and “distinctive cutlery, plates and cups that are easily identified”, which are particularly useful for shared accommodation.

“A box of store cupboard ingredients such as olive oil, soy, stock cubes and spices to use when cooking,” is also well-received, she says.

News.title: Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check
News.content:
Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

Team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Ebola outbreak ‘doubling every 20 days’, warns UN chief
News.content:
Congo’s runaway Ebola outbreak is doubling in size every 20 days, according to the United Nations humanitarian chief, putting it on track to soon be the largest ever seen.

Three months after the outbreak was officially declared, the case load is expanding exponentially and many believe the true toll is far higher than recorded.

If cases continue to double at the same rate, the flare-up in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will surpass the record West African outbreak sometime around the end of September.

Modelling by one health analytics firm already predicts there is a more than 90 per cent chance that the DRC will become the largest on record.

The two-year West African outbreak grew to more than 28,600 cases and 11,325 deaths across Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea from late 2013 to 2016.

This year’s outbreak centred on the DRC province of Ituri has already seen 4,449 cases and 2,061 deaths in only a few months.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

Sports.title: Aston Villa's dream end to transfer window as Unai Emery completes four new signings
Sports.content:
Aston Villa's dream end to transfer window as Unai Emery completes four new signings

Aston Villa could complete several key transfers in a dream end to the summer window as Unai Emery looks to strengthen his squad

View 3 Images Unai Emery is looking to improve his Aston Villa squad in the summer transfer window (Image: May JAMES / AFP via Getty Images)

Aston Villa face a pivotal few weeks in the transfer window but are just a few deals away from having a dream squad at their disposal. Unai Emery squeezed the maximum out of his squad last season by winning the Europa League and finishing fourth in the Premier League.

‌



A rebuild was necessary even before the eye-catching £117m sale of Morgan Rogers and the arguably more important loss of Youri Tielemans to Manchester United. Emery has kept the same core of players throughout his time at Villa but supporters are set to watch a team with a refreshed identity.

‌



World Cup star Johan Manzambi will take Rogers’ place as Villa’s No.10, sitting further forward than £35m arrival Joao Gomes, who will form a more combative midfield duo with Boubacar Kamara. Out wide, Emery will hope to bring the best out of Chelsea loanee Alejandro Garnacho after finally landing the 22-year-old ahead of a possible £43m move.

‌



A new left-back is also required after Lucas Digne joined Paris Saint-Germain, with the Villans also having targets in multiple other positions. Meanwhile, several of Villa’s key players have been linked with moves away. Here is a look at a dream scenario of how Villa’s transfer window could end by deadline day on September 1.

Endrick signs

A lot can change during the course of the transfer window. In a dream world, Villa should be able to seal a loan move for Endrick, despite recent reports in Spain that the Real Madrid superstar is set to stay with Los Blancos.

‌



The 20-year-old scored and assisted eight goals apiece in 21 games for Lyon last term and Villa could offer Endrick a chance to prove his worth in the Premier League. However, despite Villa’s need to add another attacking option, Endrick would not face an easy path into the team on the right flank ahead of captain John McGinn, who continues to improve under Emery.

Endrick’s arrival would also be based on Leon Bailey sealing a move away from Villa Park, having been in protracted talks over a switch to Hull City. Evann Guessand has already returned to Crystal Palace on loan.

Three other targets arrive

At left-back, Vila are closing in on a £17million move for Atletico Madrid’s Matteo Ruggeri, with the 24-year-old set to take Digne’s place in the squad. The former Atalanta star will compete with Ian Maatsen, giving Villa enviable depth on the left flank.

Midfield target Joao Palhinha ranked second in the Premier League for total tackles during his Spurs loan spell, just ahead of £35m new signing Gomes. Villa’s director of football has confirmed the club are in talks with Bayern Munich over Palhinha, who would ideally join on loan to replace the injured Amadou Onana.

‌



Cover for Matty Cash at right-back is another priority and the club have been linked with West Ham’s Aaron Wan-Bissaka. While some fans have called for 20-year-old Kosta Nedeljkovic to be given opportunities, recruiting Wan-Bissaka would give Villa experienced cover in both full-back areas.

Key trio to stay

While Villa have had to deal with high-profile departures this summer, a dream window would see the Villans keep the remaining nucleus of Emery’s successful team. In a season where nine clubs are beginning the campaign with new managers, consistency could help Villa stay ahead of their rivals.

Following his emotional farewells last year, Emi Martinez winning the Europa League could have symbolised a natural end to his time at the club. However, despite interest from Juventus, Villa would ideally keep their beloved ‘world’s number one’ and benefit from his continuity between the sticks.

Even during a frustrating campaign where he struggled for full fitness, the 30-year-old ended with 21 goals in all competitions and is the perfect forward to lead Emery’s side and could also form a new-look attack alongside Endrick.

Sports.title: Arsenal and Liverpool set for transfer tribunal after teenager signed for Gunners
Sports.content:
Arsenal and Liverpool set for transfer tribunal after teenager signed for Gunners

Liverpool have lost highly-rated 16-year-old striker Vincent Joseph to Premier League rivals Arsenal, who have been unable to reach an agreement over a settlement payment

View 2 Images Vincent Joseph is an England under-16 international (Image: Instagram/@vincent.joseph9)

Liverpool and Arsenal are set to face off in a tribunal after reportedly being unable to agree a payment for young striker Vincent Joseph.

‌



The 16-year-old has agreed to join the Gunners after leaving Liverpool last month. Joseph had been offered a scholarship contract by the Reds, yet decided to reject it and move down to north London instead.

‌



The England youth international, who had played for Liverpool's under-18s, saw his schoolboy registration contract expire. Manchester United, Chelsea, Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund were all reportedly interested in his signature.

‌



But the defending Premier League champions won the race and now owe a fee to Liverpool. Such payments are required when a youngster moves clubs before signing a professional contract.

The Daily Mail report that the two clubs have been unable to reach an agreement and will therefore see the matter settled at a tribunal. The level of compensation for Liverpool will be decided by the Professional Football Compensation Committee (PFCC).

The PFCC will be given all the details of the discussions between the two clubs, what terms they offered Joseph and his career at Liverpool previously.

Joseph has eight goals in nine appearances for England under-16s and becomes the latest high-profile case of a young player moving between Premier League sides.

‌



Back in February, Liverpool were ordered to pay Chelsea £2.8million in compensation for Rio Ngumoha. The young winger left the Blues' academy in September 2024 and later joined Liverpool, much to his ex-club's annoyance.

View 2 Images Liverpool had to pay Chelsea compensation for Rio Ngumoha (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Ngumoha had turned down contract offers from Chelsea and headed for Liverpool because he felt there was a quicker route to the first team. The 17-year-old has since made 30 appearances for the club, scoring twice and making a big impact.

‌



Joseph is one of a group of young players who have been recruited by Arsenal this summer. Mylo Bernard, 16, has joined from Crystal Palace after his schoolboy deal expired with the Eagles.

Meanwhile, Axel Donczew is reportedly poised to leave Cardiff City for Arsenal. The 16-year-old became Cardiff's youngest ever first-team player when he turned out at 15 years and 234 days in October, but is now heading to north London too.

The competition for the best young players in the country has increased in recent years, with clubs realising the potential benefits of signing and developing them early. The compensation fees involved are much smaller and easily stomached by the Premier League's Big Six.

Sports.title: Arsenal rocked by £20m Ezri Konsa problem after new transfer talks with Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Arsenal rocked by £20m Ezri Konsa problem after new transfer talks with Aston Villa

Arsenal remain strongly interested in Aston Villa and England central defender Ezri Konsa, who has two years left to run on his existing deal at Villa Park

View 2 Images Arsenal's are not currently prepared to match Aston Villa's £60m valuation for Ezri Konsa

Arsenal have been back in touch with Aston Villa over a potential deal for Ezri Konsa but the UEFA Super Cup finalists' £60million valuation is proving problematic.

‌



The 28-year-old remains the Premier League champions' top defensive target heading into the final stretch of the summer transfer window with head coach Mikel Arteta actively pushing to strengthen his backline.

‌



For now, there remains a notable gap - worth in the region of £20m - between what the Gunners would be willing to pay and the kind of money that would see Villa seriously consider a sale.

‌



Arsenal are understood to have made a verbal approach for Konsa earlier in the window, around the time of their interest in Morgan Rogers, which ultimately amounted to nothing.

But the Gunners never truly threw in the towel as the versatile centre-back, who can also operate as a right-back, ticks multiple boxes Arteta.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He is rapidly approaching his peak and is vastly experienced having just competed in his second major tournament for England. He is also a threat in both boxes and crucially, is homegrown.

Konsa, who is also close friends with Bukayo Saka, hails from Newham in east London and is thought to be open to joining Arsenal, even though he was a boyhood Tottenham Hotspur supporter.

Still, a transfer, at this stage, remains difficult as Unai Emery is counting on the player for the upcoming season.

‌



Villa have also offered Konsa a new contract, his existing deal expires in 2028, and that proposal remains on the table.

Mirror Football understands Arsenal would be prepared to better the wages currently on offer in the Midlands, which may prove attractive for Konsa

Villa are not thought to be under any immediate financial pressure to cash-in following the exits of Rogers (£117m to Chelsea ) and Youri Tielemans (£35m to Manchester United) and there's a desire to strengthen, not weaken, Emery's squad following the 2-1 defeat to PSG in Salzburg.

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal are in the hunt for Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa (Image: (Photo by Sarah Stier - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

For now, Arsenal view 16-year-old Marli Salmon is viewed as adequate cover and competition for Cristhian Mosquera at right centre-back but there is still scope to bolster their defensive options without William Saliba sidelined due to a back issue.

An injury to Ben White or Mosquera, would also drastically change the picture with Jurrien Timber still recovering from a minor groin procedure.

‌



Ideally, the Gunners want to sign a profile that can play at both centre-back and right-back, which is why Konsa fits the bill.

Other options, including Tottenham's Cristian Romero (now set to join Atletico Madrid) and Atletico's Marc Pubill have been explored but to no avail. Arsenal will be forced to consider other alternatives if Villa continue to dig their heels into the ground.

Konsa has been handed an extended break by Emery alongside England team-mate Ollie Watkins and goalkeeper Emi Martinez following their involvement in the World Cup. He has insisted that all three players required four weeks of rest, which is why he ruled them out of the Super Cup.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick tells Man Utd owners exactly what he needs in rest of transfer window
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick tells Man Utd owners exactly what he needs in rest of transfer window

Manchester United have gone a month without announcing a transfer in the summer window and manager Michael Carrick has urged the hierarchy to get deals over the line

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is keen for new players at Manchester United (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has sent a clear message to the Manchester United hierarchy by telling them to "keep pushing" for more transfers this summer.

‌



United have signed Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, from Aston Villa and Chelsea respectively, to strengthen their midfield, while Karl Darlow arrived from Leeds on a free transfer to become the back-up goalkeeper. But their total expenditure of £85million lags way behind their Premier League rivals.

‌



It has now been a month since United announced a new signing and, with just 19 days left until the transfer deadline on September 1 and nine until United's first game of the 2026/27 season, Carrick has made his feelings clear.

‌



"I think we've got a pretty good balance in all when you lay the squad out, but we would like more, we need to keep pushing for more," he told the Manchester Evening News.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"There's one or two areas where we'd like to improve and we feel that there's the possibility to improve, but again, that needs to be something that we can do that makes us better and improves the group, whether that's quality or whether that's a little bit of depth. That's something we've got to manage. That's pretty obvious."

Carrick wants to sign a left-back to compete with Luke Shaw, with Newcastle's Lewis Hall the top target, as well as another central midfielder. His squad only had to compete in the Premier League following his arrival as interim boss in January to replace Ruben Amorim and Carrick knows the upcoming campaign will be more demanding, with United back in the Champions League and cup competitions.

This summer has seen huge transfer fees become even more normalised, with Morgan Rogers, Elliot Anderson and Sandro Tonali all moving for £100m or more. Remarkably, United's record transfer remains the £89m they paid Juventus for Paul Pogba in 2016.

‌



View 2 Images Andrey Santos has impressed Michael Carrick since his £50m transfer (Image: Michael Campanella/Getty Images)

Asked if United may need to break that record this summer, Carrick said: "A little bit depends on what position that is and what you've got and what dynamics you need at certain points. Sometimes you do need that if it's the right player.

"Again, it's not purely on money, the money doesn't guarantee you, it needs to be the right player and a better player for what we've got. It's something [that] over time we need to be pushing to look to enhance the squad all the time in different ways."

‌



Carrick has been delighted by the impact that Santos, in particular, has made since joining for £50m from Chelsea. And he stressed that communication with director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada remains good.

"It's constant communication of where, what work we need to do, where we want to improve," he said. "We're pretty clear in the messages that we need to keep pushing and there's certain things that we want to try and do, but it needs to be right as well."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick confirms Man Utd's Marcus Rashford plan as transfer reality becomes clear
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick confirms Man Utd's Marcus Rashford plan as transfer reality becomes clear

Marcus Rashford has returned to Manchester United following loan spells with Aston Villa and Barcelona as Michael Carrick prepares to reintegrate him into the squad

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford is back in the Manchester United picture

Michael Carrick insists Marcus Rashford still has plenty to offer Manchester United this season with it now looking increasingly likely he will stay at Old Trafford.

‌



The England international hasn't played for his boyhood club since December 2024, when he was frozen out by former manager Ruben Amorim. Since then, he has had loan spells with Aston Villa and then spent last season with Barcelona.

‌



It was expected that he would secure a permanent move to the Camp Nou, but their decision to sign Anthony Gordon meant they opted against triggering his £26million clause.

‌



He now returns to United, where he could make his return, ironically, against Amorim's AC Milan this weekend. The Manchester Evening News report both sides believe it is most likely he will remain at his parent club and Carrick is confident he will be a positive presence in his squad.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"He's a very good player, and I think if you're going to have a career over 10 or 15 years, there's going to be times when things go in a direction and maybe a different direction," he said.

‌



"I think there are ups and downs, and that doesn't judge you as a one-off kind of judgment. It's what happens over time, and now we're in a positive place as a group, and Marcus can offer us so much. He has done, and he can do again, so in that respect, it's quite exciting."

Had Amorim stayed in charge, it is inconceivable that the burnt bridges would have been able to be mended, but Carrick has a history with Rashford and has helped to smooth the process.

And while Carrick stopped short of definitively confirming he will stay at United, he described him as 'our player' and said he is being treated the same as anyone else within his squad.

‌



View 2 Images Rashford has not played for Manchester United since December 2024 (Image: Getty Images)

"He's our player, he came back Sunday night, he arrived with Kobbie [Mainoo], and Lisandro [Martinez] came the day after, and he's part of the group like anybody else. He came in, he's trained really well.

"I've known him a long time, like I've known some of the others a long time, so I don't treat him any different to anybody else, but it's been good to have him around the group again this week. So I'm really positive with that."

‌



Carrick added that he was confident the returning Rashford would bring something new to his options and help balance the squad for the upcoming Premier League campaign.

He added: "We're really calm, we just treat it like anybody else coming into the group and there's obviously this slight twist that he knows the club as well as anybody and that's a real positive.

‌



"He's been here all his career, all his life before the last 18 months or so, to understand what it means. That side of things is natural, that's a given. I know he's got history, but I've got history with a number of the players as well, so that doesn't make that a unique situation at all and treat him as exactly like any other player.

"Bringing him into the group and carrying on as normal brings the good things that we haven't got, and we want to get that balance with every individual player, and Marcus has come back and he's in good form, and it's been good to have him around this week."

Sports.title: Swiatek beats Rybakina to end title drought in Toronto
Sports.content:
Iga Swiatek claimed her first title of the season with a dominant 6-2 6-3 win over Elena Rybakina in the final of the National Bank Open in Toronto.

The Polish seventh seed gained an early advantage in the first set when the world No 2 gave up a break point on back-to-back double faults.

That was all the room Swiatek needed as she continued her stellar form from earlier in the tournament to race away with the opening set.

Unforced errors continued to cost Rybakina into the second set, as two missed backhands gifted Swiatek another break.

Rybakina was able to stave off one championship point, but Swiatek converted on her second opportunity to clinch her first title since last September.

Speaking at the post-match awards ceremony, Swiatek dedicated her victory to "everyone who is dealing with unfair judgement and hate".

She said: "Just keep pushing, keep growing, keep focusing on yourself because you know what's best for you.

"Always remember what's ahead and what might be possible."

Shelton retains crown

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Canadian Open men's final between Ben Shelton and Brandon Nakashima.

In the men's draw, American Ben Shelton retained his crown by eclipsing compatriot Brandon Nakashima 6-3 7-6 (7-4) in Montreal.

Shelton did not drop a set throughout the tournament and is just the fourth man this century to go back-to-back at the event, joining Andy Murray, Novak Djokovic and Rafael Nadal.

Image: Ben Shelton completed his flawless Canadian Open title defence with victory over Brandon Nakashima

He told atptour.com: "For me to play the way that I played this week to go through this draw speaks to the work I have been putting in.

"It also speaks to my mental toughness, my ability to focus through everything that was going on this week."

Sports.title: Super League leaders Leeds beaten by Leigh after late drama
Sports.content:
Innes Senior scored twice as Leigh Leopards inflicted a first home defeat of the season on Betfred Super League leaders Leeds Rhinos by winning 20-16 at Headingley.

Wing Senior went over twice in the first half after team-mate Josh Charnley's effort had cancelled out Ryan Hall's opener for Leeds, for whom Brodie Croft also touched down before the break.

In balmy, energy-sapping conditions after the hottest day in the UK this year, Leigh scored a fourth try through centre Umyla Hanley early in the second period and then withstood heavy pressure to seal a deserved win.

Ryan Hall thought his late effort for Leeds had tied the scores, but his foot was clearly in touch as he grounded the ball in the corner and Leigh clung on.

Hall touched down in the corner for the opening try in the second minute after taking Jake Connor's quick pass following a high kick, but Leigh's response was immediate as Charnley raced over following Hanley's line break.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Leigh Leopards head coach Adrian Lam reflects on their Super League win at Leeds Rhinos.

Connor's penalty in front of the posts for a shoulder barge on Kallum Watkins edged Leeds 8-6 ahead, but Leigh piled on the pressure midway through the first half and got their reward.

Senior powered over near the touchline and despite Leeds full-back Lachlan Miller's brilliant tackle, the video referee ruled the Leigh winger had dotted down before going out of bounds to put his side 10-8 up.

Leeds came roaring back when Croft burst through a gap under the posts for a converted score to nudge them 14-10 in front.

Rhinos centre Jack Bird went off for a head injury assessment following a clattering tackle and was replaced by teenager Zak Lloyd, whose terrific last-ditch tackle halted Charnley soon after.

But quick hands saw Leigh spin the ball left for Senior to go over on the outside to level the scores at 14-14 at half-time after Cook had missed his second conversion attempt.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Leeds Rhinos head coach Brad Arthur reflects on their Super League defeat to Leigh Leopards.

Connor landed his second penalty to give Leeds a two-point advantage soon after the restart following Cook's off-the-ball block on Ash Handley.

Leigh responded again though, carving open the Rhinos' defence via another slick handling move that sent Hanley over for the visitors' fourth try of the match, with Cook adding the extras to put them 20-16 in front.

The visitors were reduced to 12 men when second row Andy Badrock was sin-binned for his dangerous tackle on Harry Newman with 17 minutes to go.

Leeds threatened to make their extra man count, but they lacked composure and failed to execute in the face of some desperate, scrambling defending from Leigh.

Image: Umyla Hanley (R) celebrates scoring Leigh's final try

With three minutes remaining, Leeds thought they had drawn level when Handley sent Hall over in the corner following Connor's high kick.

But the video referee revealed the winger's foot was in touch as he grounded the ball and Leigh held firm before celebrating an impressive win.

Leeds' defeat gives Wigan Warriors the chance to move level with them at the top of the table on 36 points when they visit struggling Bradford Bulls on Sunday.

The victory kept Leigh on course for the playoffs as they tightened their grip on sixth by moving six points clear of St Helens, who can claim a maximum of 10 points from their five remaining games.

Warrington beat York to go third

Warrington Wolves beat York Knights 30-10 at the Halliwell Jones Stadium to move back up to third.

York had taken an early lead after Warrington failed to deal with a high kick and Paul McShane went over in the corner.

The Wolves - looking to edge ahead above play-off rivals Wakefield - then got themselves in front after nine minutes when Josh Thewlis darted through to slide in under the posts and Ewan Irwin added the extras.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League clash between Warrington Wolves and York Knights.

The Knights, though, soon responded again when Cody Hunter's low kick was not gathered by the Warrington backline and Jon Bennison latched onto the loose ball in the right corner.

Sam Stone, returning to the side following a three-month injury lay-off, chased George Williams' kick on the left wing and dived full length to just touch the ball down as he slid off into the advertising boards, before 18-year-old Irwin scored a fine individual try, stepping inside to burst clear, and his penalty then put Warrington 18-10 ahead at half-time.

York were punished for giving away penalties early in the second half when hooker Danny Walker took the ball a couple of yards out to spin under the posts.

Image: Ewan Irwin (R) celebrates scoring one of Warrington's five tries

Irwin then picked up a loose ball to sprint clear and run in a 60-yard try - but his celebrations were cut short after a lengthy video review decided James Bentley had knocked Denive Balmforth's arm, which caused him to fumble possession.

After a breakaway from Hunter, which looked set for a York try, was called back for what looked a tight offside call, Warrington made sure when Aaron Lindop went over in the corner after Albert Hopoate had tapped back a high kick and Irwin then slotted over a late penalty.

Hull KR maintained their push for a home play-off with a comfortable 28-10 victory over Catalans Dragons.

The home side led 22-6 after a dominant first half that saw Jack Broadbent touch down twice as Jez Litten and Joe Burgess also scored.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League clash between Hull KR and Catalans Dragons.

Tyrone May all but sealed victory with the first score of the second half after 62 minutes, before Tommy Makinson hit back with a late consolation try for Catalans.

The victory kept Hull ahead of Leigh in fifth on points difference, and moved them within just two points of Warrington and Wakefield in third and fourth.

Sports.title: Gay out for duck as Pakistan impress against County Select XI
Sports.content:
England opening batter Emilio Gay was out for a duck as Pakistan made a strong start to their tour against a Professional County Club Select XI.

Concerns over Gay's fitness for England's first Test against Pakistan, which starts on August 19, were allayed by the left-hander's inclusion for the game at Beckenham, but he made the worst possible start.

The 27-year-old, who had suffered a shoulder issue playing for Durham last week, was caught off the bowling of Mohammad Abbas by Salan Agha at second slip, having failed to score from his 12 balls faced.

PCCSXI would go on to be bowled out for 305, with captain Tom Haines, Caleb Falconer and Saif Zaib contributing half-centuries before Matthew Fisher, who is in England's 16-player squad for the first two Tests against Pakistan, made a crucial unbeaten 62 batting at 10.

James Rew, who made his England Test debut against New Zealand in June, was also dismissed cheaply as he fell for just four to Abbas.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England Test captain Joe Root explains why he has removed the curfew that was previously imposed on his team.

Abbas (3-37) and Mohammad Ali (3-23) were the pick of the Pakistan bowlers, while Khurram Shahzad (2-55) also chipped with a couple of wickets despite being more expensive.

There was also a wicket apiece for Aamer Jamal (1-32) and Ali Usman (1-38).

Pakistan then put themselves in a strong position in the three-day contest by reaching 44-0 at the close, with Azan Awais (15*) and Imam-ul-Haq (26*) seeing out the final 13 overs of the day.

Fisher was economical as he went for just seven runs from his four overs, while the other PCCSXI player who is in England's Test squad, spinner Shoaib Bashir, bowled two overs at the end of the day.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England selector Marcus North reflects on the latest decisions around the Test side and explains the involvement of Stephen Fleming.

Both sides are fielding more than XI players in the match, with Pakistan attempting to give as many of their touring squad as possible match practice ahead of Tests at Headingley, Lord's and Edgbaston.

England will be led captained by Joe Root following his reappointment as captain after Ben Stokes retired from international cricket during the final Test of the 2-1 series defeat to New Zealand in June.

England also have a new head coach in Stephen Fleming, who has replaced Brendon McCullum but is not taking charge of the side during the Pakistan series, for which Marcus Trescothick will be in interim charge.
